statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 21 sits in the watch band after the cash Nasdaq-100 bounced off its 30,264.51 session low and reclaimed the 30,276.81 prior close, resolving the failed retracement recorded an hour earlier. Stress 75 stays high because the thirty-year yield is at 5.61%, its highest since 2002.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold at 21, so the deterministic mapping stays at WATCH with a yellow status. The single elevated-band window on the horizon is the 12:00 to 15:00 UTC block on September 30 covering ADP, core PCE, the US cash open and Chicago PMI, where conditional Tail peaks at 28.
headline: Cash NDX recovers 47 points from its 30,264.51 session low to 30,311.76, back above the prior close, as the 30-year yield reaches 5.61% and WTI falls 2.4% to 90.42; the completed retracement eases Tail to 21
body: The clearest current evidence is the cash Nasdaq-100. It opened at 30,412.29, made an early 30,429.97 high, fell through its 30,276.81 prior close to a 30,264.51 session low after the 14:00 UTC data block, and has now recovered to 30,311.76, up 34.95 points or 0.12% and about 47 points above the low. That matters because an hour ago the same index was sitting on the low with a 64-point bounce given back; the retracement has since completed and the index trades above the prior close. A completed retracement is the opposite of the Tail amplifier recorded at 15:36 UTC, which is why Tail falls from 24 to 21 rather than rising. The total cash range remains 165.46 points, or 0.55%, so there is still no meaningful directional displacement to extend. NQ front-month futures trade 30,564.50, down 1.75 points or 0.01% against a 30,566.25 prior close, having covered 30,372.25 to 30,725.50 and visited both extremes with retracements, which is two-way rather than one-way behaviour. The live amplifier is duration and it has pressed further. The ten-year trades 5.28%, up four basis points from a 5.24% prior close and one basis point below its 5.29% session high, while the thirty-year has reached 5.61% against a 5.56% prior close, within a basis point of its 5.62% session high and reported today as the highest since 2002. Reporting attributes the long-end selloff to elevated energy prices, heavy corporate supply and expectations of a further Federal Reserve hike after the September 16 increase; the New York Fed president said last week that another hike by year end is reasonable. That duration move is the reason Stress stays at 75 and the reason Tail does not fall further. Implied volatility has still not confirmed a pathological path: VIX trades 16.26, up 0.19 points or 1.18%, inside a 15.73 to 16.43 range, a session high but a historically low absolute level. The cross-asset picture is divergent rather than aligned. The Dow is down about 0.58% and the S&P 500 about 0.26% while the Nasdaq-100 is higher, so index-level breadth conflicts, and under the risk contract conflicting evidence raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than mechanically raising Tail. Crude has fallen further, with WTI down 2.36% to 90.42 and Brent down 1.18% to 104.04 on the Saudi East-West pipeline restart and continuing United States and Iran mediation, which removes an inflationary input and partly offsets the yield move. Today's data was weak and was absorbed: Conference Board consumer confidence fell to 81.9 against an 89.2 consensus, its lowest since 2014, with the present situation index at 109.3 and expectations at 63.6, August JOLTS job openings printed 7.079 million against a 7.23 million consensus, and the Dallas Fed services index came in at -1.8, while Case-Shiller home prices rose 2.5% year over year and the FHFA index reached 443.5. Technology headline flow is mixed: a leaked Anthropic listing prospectus and a shelved OpenAI frontier model have fuelled AI-safety jitters, while AMD's 8.2 billion dollar acquisition of World Labs and a fully positive semiconductor complex support the sector. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 14:22 UTC and is therefore about two hours old, outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so it was treated as stale supporting context only. Its collection status is partial with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, and its breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are explicitly labelled latest-session and non-real-time, so they cannot establish current NQ structure in any case. Those sections did corroborate the divergence already established independently, with all seven tracked semiconductors positive at a mean change near 1.9% against only three of eight megacaps positive. Every price, yield, volatility, oil and release figure above comes from independent current research fetched within the last few minutes, and every headline sourced from the Finviz feed was treated as discovery only and verified before use. The net picture is high but decaying Stress, one live duration amplifier at a 24-year extreme, a completed rather than failed retracement, conflicting cross-asset breadth and no persistent one-way structure of any size, which places Tail at 21.

lookbackSummary: 23 of the 24 preceding hours were published; the 14:00 UTC slot is unavailable because no Claude assessment was published in that clock hour. Tail ranged from 17 to 24 across the available hours and never reached the elevated band. Tail troughed at 17 through the late Monday and early Tuesday overnight session, printed 24 at 01:00, 03:00 and 04:00 UTC during the European handover as the long-end selloff was repriced, held 20 to 21 through the European and early US morning, then printed 24 again in the 15:00 UTC hour when the cash index was sitting on its session low with a failed bounce. Stress declined from 80 to 74 before ticking back to 76. Confidence held between 86 and 88 throughout. The dominant mode was mixed for 14 hours, normal for 4 hours and trend-down for 4 hours, with one trend-up hour at 12:00 UTC.
outlookSummary: The published forecast keeps Tail at 21 for the current hour, where a completed retracement above the prior close is actually observed, then holds the watch-band floor through the September 29 afternoon and into the low band across the US evening and early Asian overnight window, which is the pattern the lookback recorded a day earlier. Tail returns to the watch band from the Asian morning onward and builds gradually as positioning for the September 30 release block develops. The horizon contains one elevated-band window of three hours, from 12:00 to 14:00 UTC on September 30: the 12:15 UTC ADP employment change and the 12:30 UTC block of August core PCE, personal spending, the third estimate of Q2 GDP and the advance goods trade balance; the delayed second leg into the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC Chicago PMI, where conditional Tail peaks at 28; and the post-open hour containing the 14:30 UTC EIA crude stocks change. Stress is forecast to decay from 75 to 69 overnight before rebuilding to 80 into the release block, and Confidence steps down from 88 to 74 across the horizon as the current price-path evidence ages. Every hour beyond the current clock hour describes a conditional path rather than observed structure.
